newsitem.title: USA: Canadian crude cuts, Odessa troubles aid US grades.
newsitem.headline: Canadian crude cuts, Odessa troubles aid US grades.

text.p: Supply cuts aided U.S. cash crude grade prices Friday afternoon, though outright benchmark levels faded to slight losses.
At 1528 EDT (1928 GMT), September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood one cent lower at $20.00-20.10 a barrel, with the September/October spread at -20 cents.

Slack market conditions prevented much price volatility, but traders said there was at least some movement on news Canada's IPL Energy will slice pipeline throughputs 141,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold into $1.25 under September WTYI, but since moved back to a $1.30/25 cents discount.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talked between 20-25 cents over the marker. Relatively tight WTI-Brent spreads continued to bolster sweet domestic grades, traders said.
Midland/WTI was impacted slightly by word Shell's refinery in Odessa, Texas idled a crude distillation unit after a fire on Wednesday.
